difference: `end - start` on wall-clock minutes is negative for 22:00 to 06:00 and for an end at 00:00, and the total shrinks. When the end is earlier than the start, add 1440 minutes. These are planned wall-clock minutes; elapsed time across a clock change needs the zone.
intent: Give the planned minutes of each event of the planning export, given its start and end times; an event may end after midnight.
title: A time range that ends before it starts ends the next day · WRONG_OUTCOME

difference: Grouping by `.in_reply_to // .id` stops after one hop: a reply to a reply opens a new group named after its parent. Follow the parent while it is in the batch (bounded by the number of messages) and group by that root.
intent: Group the new messages by conversation: a reply to a reply belongs to the same conversation, and replies to a message outside the batch stay together.
title: A conversation follows reply chains to their root · WRONG_OUTCOME

difference: Addresses are compared as typed: `Ana@Acme.EXAMPLE` and ` bob@bolt.example ` miss their directory entries, and two entries that differ only by case are taken as two keys, so a conflicting match is filled instead of reported. Index and look up with `ascii_downcase | trim` (A to Z only: ascii_downcase leaves other letters such as É unchanged).
intent: Fill the missing company of each prospect from the supplier directory by e-mail address; keep a company already in the CRM and report the prospects left unmatched or matched twice.
title: A typed key matches without letter case or surrounding spaces · WRONG_OUTCOME

difference: `sort_by(.urgency) | reverse` puts equal urgencies in reverse arrival order, so the latest message wins a tie and a cut at the top N keeps the wrong ones. `max_by` also returns the last of equals. Sort by `-.urgency` then by arrival time; jq's sort_by is stable.
intent: List the most urgent messages to answer first, the earliest arrival first among equal urgency, and name the very first one.
title: Ranking keeps equal scores in arrival order · WRONG_OUTCOME

difference: Each day and the window are closed at both ends (`<=`). A sale paid exactly at midnight counts in two days, and a sale at today's midnight enters a window that ends before today. Use `start <= t and t < end`; an instant compares as a number, whatever offset its text carries.
intent: Count the paid sales of each of the 14 UTC days before today, and of the whole window.
title: A window of days is half-open: start included, next start excluded · WRONG_OUTCOME

difference: Cutting `received_at[0:7]` reads the UTC month: an attachment received at 00:30 on the 1st in Paris, 22:00 on 31 December in New York or 00:30 on the 1st in Kolkata lands in the wrong folder. Convert the instant with nika:date (op format, the IANA zone) before taking the month.
intent: File each billing attachment under the year and month it was received in the person's time zone.
title: A day or a month is read in the person's zone · WRONG_OUTCOME
